# SVG Vector Lab

> SVG Vector Lab is a free, open-source SVG editor that runs in the browser. It provides visual path and shape editing alongside live SVG source, keeps artwork on the user's device, and exports standard SVG or PNG files.

SVG Vector Lab is available at https://svgvectorlab.com. It requires no signup or installation. The hosted editor is free to use, and the source code is licensed under the MIT License.

## Product

- [SVG Vector Lab Editor](https://svgvectorlab.com/): Open the visual SVG editor and edit SVG paths, points, shapes, attributes, transforms, fill, and stroke.
- [Editor Features](https://svgvectorlab.com/free-svg-editor/): Review the privacy model, supported editing tools, exports, and common questions before opening the editor.
- [Edit SVG Online](https://svgvectorlab.com/edit-svg-online/): Start with a blank SVG and edit visually or through synchronized source.
- [SVG Path Editor](https://svgvectorlab.com/svg-path-editor/): Edit anchors, Bézier handles, path commands, and coordinates.
- [Convert SVG Shapes to Paths](https://svgvectorlab.com/convert-shapes-to-paths/): Convert basic SVG elements into editable path data.
- [Convert SVG to PNG](https://svgvectorlab.com/svg-to-png/): Preview and export SVG as PNG at multiple resolutions.
- [About SVG Vector Lab](https://svgvectorlab.com/about/): Project purpose, principles, local processing, supported SVG elements, and open-source licensing.

## SVG Guides

- [SVG Guide Library](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/): Index of practical SVG tutorials.
- [SVG viewBox Explained](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/svg-viewbox/): Coordinate systems, responsive scaling, aspect ratio, zoom, whitespace, and cropping.
- [Edit SVG Paths](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/edit-svg-paths/): Path commands, anchors, control points, subpaths, and editing workflow.
- [Understand Bezier Curves](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/bezier-curves/): Cubic curves, C and S commands, handles, and smooth curve construction.
- [Convert Shapes to Paths](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/convert-shapes-to-paths/): When and how to convert SVG shapes into editable path data.
- [Optimize SVG](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/optimize-svg/): Reduce unnecessary SVG markup while preserving appearance and accessibility.
- [SVG Path Commands](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/path-commands/): Read move, line, curve, arc, and close commands, including relative coordinates.
- [SVG Transforms](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/svg-transforms/): Understand transform order, pivot points, nested groups, and matrices.
- [SVG Strokes](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/svg-strokes/): Control stroke width, linecaps, joins, dash patterns, and scaling.
- [SVG Gradients](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/svg-gradients/): Build linear and radial gradients with deliberate units, stops, and reusable IDs.
- [Accessible SVG](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/svg-accessibility/): Choose text alternatives, titles, focus behavior, contrast, and motion settings.
- [Responsive SVG](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/responsive-svg/): Combine viewBox, CSS sizing, intrinsic ratio, and embedding methods.
- [SVG Clipping and Masking](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/clipping-and-masking/): Choose hard clips or soft masks and debug their bounds and coordinate systems.
- [Debug Invisible SVG](https://svgvectorlab.com/guides/debug-invisible-svg/): Isolate size, viewBox, paint, geometry, transforms, references, and effects.
